title: Never disclose authentication secrets to an unknown caller
text: Do not share OTPs, passwords, PINs, CVV values, card details, or internet-banking credentials with an unknown caller, even when the caller claims to represent a bank, regulator, police department, or government office. Independently contact the institution using a number or channel you already trust.

title: Threats to freeze or block an account can be impersonation tactics
text: A caller or message that threatens to freeze, block, or deactivate an account and then asks for OTPs, PINs, passwords, card information, KYC documents, money, or an app installation has multiple high-risk indicators. Do not comply under pressure; verify through your bank's official channel.
license_note: Paraphrased summary; consult the linked source for authoritative wording.

title: Do not pay fees to claim a prize or promised government/RBI funds
text: Be suspicious of offers that promise a lottery win, unexpected grant, government benefit, or large transfer but require an upfront processing fee, security deposit, customs charge, or release payment. Verify independently and do not send money solely because the caller claims to be an official.
license_note: Paraphrased summary; consult the linked source for authoritative wording.

title: A UPI PIN is not needed to receive money
text: Entering a UPI PIN authorizes a payment; it is not required merely to receive money. Be cautious if someone asks you to scan a QR code, click a cashback link, or enter a UPI PIN to receive a refund, reward, or payment.
license_note: Paraphrased summary; consult the linked source for authoritative wording.

title: Do not open suspicious links or install apps at a caller's request
text: Unexpected links, remote-access applications, or requests to install an unverified application are risk indicators, especially when paired with pressure, threats, or requests for banking information. Stop the interaction and independently verify the request using an official channel.
license_note: Paraphrased summary; consult the linked source for authoritative wording.

title: Verify KYC requests through your bank's official channel
text: A KYC reminder alone does not prove fraud. Treat demands for OTPs, PINs, passwords, card details, payment, or immediate action through an unknown link or caller as suspicious. Contact the bank through a verified channel rather than using contact details supplied by the unsolicited message.
license_note: Paraphrased summary; consult the linked source for authoritative wording.

title: Act quickly after a suspected unauthorised transaction
text: If money may have been transferred without permission, contact your bank immediately. India’s public cyber-safety guidance also points people to the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and cybercrime helpline 1930. The user should verify current reporting instructions from the official portal.
source_name: Reserve Bank of India / National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal reference
license_note: Paraphrased summary; confirm current reporting details with the official portal.

title: A request for information is not enough by itself to classify a call as fraud
text: Risk assessment should rely on the complete context, concrete actions requested, and supporting evidence. A message mentioning KYC, a bank, a transaction, or an OTP can be legitimate in some contexts. Express uncertainty when evidence is incomplete and do not claim that a caller is fraudulent based only on one keyword.
